name: Seg-XRes-CAM (eXtreme Resolution CAM for segmentation)
what: Layer-aggregated attention/CAM method that produces spatially local saliency regions for segmentation models instead of a single global heatmap, tying explanations to the pixels that drove each class decision.
why_better: Old plan uses SHAP-only (classification-style) XAI, which cannot attribute the soma/neurite mask decision to specific image regions; Seg-XRes-CAM gives segmentation-native, per-region attributions so a reviewer can verify masks come from actual cell structures rather than background cues.
evidence: Method paper metrics unverified (abstract not retrieved); a 2025 case study using it on cerebrovascular segmentation quantified attention-vs-GT overlap, reporting attention-GT IoU ~0.101 at 0.3 threshold vs attention-vs-own-prediction IoU ~0.282 under domain shift (RSNA->TopCoW), demonstrating it detects spurious-correlation failure.
source_title: Seg-XRes-CAM: Explaining Spatially Local Regions in Image Segmentation (CVPRW 2023, Hasany, Petitjean, Meriaudeau)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results)
license: unknown (IEEE CVPRW, closed access per OpenAlex)
fit_small_data: high - fully post-hoc on any trained segmentation model; no extra labelled data required.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - needs intermediate feature/attention tensors exported from the ONNX graph (graph surgery on U-Net/Swin heads); forward pass itself unchanged.
risk: Unverified for Swin-Transformer multi-task heads; exporting all decoder attention maps may bloat the ONNX model and slow CPU inference on large microscopy tiles.

name: MiSuRe (Minimally Sufficient Region saliency for segmentation)
what: Saliency algorithm for image segmentation that iteratively removes irrelevant regions until only the minimally sufficient regions for the segmentation decision remain; also used as a post-hoc reliability indicator for the segmentation model.
why_better: Beats the old plan's SHAP-only pipeline with a sufficiency criterion: a mask whose prediction survives removal of non-highlighted regions is a defensible basis for extracting morphometry, and the sufficiency score gives a per-cell reliability gate before NTI computation (SHAP gives neither).
evidence: Evaluated on Triangle (synthetic), COCO-2017 and Synapse multi-organ datasets; quantitative scores unverified (abstract only).
source_title: MiSuRe is all you need to explain your image segmentation (arXiv:2406.12173, Hasany, Meriaudeau, Petitjean)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results)
fit_small_data: high - post-hoc, works on the existing 70-image labelled set with no retraining.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - iterative masking requires many repeated forward passes per image, so per-tile wall time multiplies.
risk: Iterative removal loop is CPU-expensive on full-resolution phase-contrast tiles; convergence threshold for 'minimally sufficient' is task-specific and needs validation on labelled neurite masks.

name: CRAFT (Concept Recursive Activation FacTorization)
what: Concept-based explanation method that recursively detects and decomposes human-meaningful concepts across network layers, estimates concept importance with Sobol indices, and produces Concept Attribution Maps (both 'what' and 'where'), extending the TCAV concept-vector line of work with faithfulness-improved importance estimation.
why_better: Old plan's SHAP-only XAI names features but not biology: CRAFT yields concepts like 'branching neurite' or 'shrunken soma' with spatial maps and Sobol-based faithfulness, directly supporting the toxicity mechanism story (dose x time) that SHAP feature attributions cannot express.
evidence: Human utility and CV experiments reported; concept importance claimed more faithful than prior methods; specific numbers unverified (abstract only).
source_title: CRAFT: Concept Recursive Activation FacTorization for Explainability (arXiv:2211.10154, Fel et al.)
license: unknown (GitHub repo linked in abstract; license not checked)
fit_small_data: medium - concept mining from the 70 labelled images is small-scale; concept positives can be derived from existing soma/neurite masks and crops.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - requires per-layer activations and Sobol sampling; feasible but adds forward-pass cost.
risk: Concept discovery on only 70 annotated images may be underpowered; Sobol sampling cost scales with number of concepts; ONNX activation hooks for the multi-task Swin head must be engineered.

name: TCAV (Testing with Concept Activation Vectors)
what: Quantifies how much a prediction depends on a user-defined concept (e.g. 'thin branching neurite') via directional derivatives against concept activation vectors trained on small positive/negative concept sets.
why_better: Adds a hypothesis-test layer missing from the old plan's SHAP-only XAI: one can formally test 'does the NTI prediction depend on the branch-angle concept' and report p-value-like sensitivity scores, which SHAP attribution cannot express and which reviewers of a toxicity assay will ask for.
evidence: unverified (abstract only; classic 2017/ICML-2018 method, no segmentation-specific numbers).
source_title: Interpretability Beyond Feature Attribution: Quantitative Testing with Concept Activation Vectors (TCAV) (arXiv:1711.11279, Kim et al.)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results; reference implementations exist but unverified here)
fit_small_data: medium - CAVs need only tens of concept-positive/negative crops, derivable from existing neurite/soma annotations.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - needs internal layer activations for CAV direction computation; CAV training itself is trivial on CPU.
risk: 2017 method predates 2023-2026 preference; directional-derivative CAVs are known to be unstable for multi-concept, non-convex feature spaces; concept definition burden falls on the biology team.

name: Post-hoc Concept Bottleneck Models (pCBB)
what: Inserts a concept-prediction bottleneck on top of a frozen pretrained model, rerouting its predictions through human-auditable concepts without retraining the backbone (post-hoc version of Concept Bottleneck Models, arXiv:2007.04612).
why_better: Old plan's 'linear NTI then small NN' is a black box over morphometry; pCBB forces the pipeline through named concepts (soma area, neurite length, branch count, dose/time context) so the toxicity index is auditable per concept and intervenable (fix a concept, see the NTI change) - something SHAP post-hoc cannot do.
evidence: unverified (title/identifier confirmed via OpenAlex for arXiv:2205.15480; no metric details retrieved).
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results)
fit_small_data: medium - concept labels for soma/neurite attributes come for free from existing masks; bottleneck is small and trainable on 70 samples, but concept-label quality dominates.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - final model is a small linear bottleneck on top of the frozen encoder; ONNX export is straightforward.
risk: Original paper targets classification; adapting the bottleneck to a continuous NTI regression is unverified; forcing information through a few concepts may measurably degrade NTI accuracy.

name: PAnS (Prototype-based Anomaly Segmentation)
what: Lightweight prototype classifier over a segmentation encoder: anomalous pixels are those dissimilar to all learned class prototypes (cosine similarity), achieving state-of-the-art anomaly segmentation on StreetHazards with reduced overhead vs generative methods.
why_better: Old plan has no out-of-distribution guard: debris, out-of-focus cells or staining artifacts would silently corrupt the 4 morphometric parameters and NTI; PAnS adds a per-pixel known/unknown signal (prototypes are themselves interpretable) without labelling negatives, which a 70-image budget cannot afford.
evidence: StreetHazards dataset, reported as new state of the art over previous anomaly segmentation with reduced computational overhead; exact AUC/IOU numbers unverified (abstract only).
source_title: Detecting Anomalies in Semantic Segmentation with Prototypes (SAIAD CVPRW 2021, Fontanel, Cermelli, Mancini, Caputo)
fit_small_data: high - prototypes are mean-pixel statistics of training data; no generative model and no extra labelled negatives.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - adds only a cosine-similarity prototype head to the existing segmentation network.
risk: Prototype quality with ~70 labelled images is the key unknown; the paper's setup is street-scene binary+anomaly, so adaptation to soma/neurite/artifact classes needs its own validation.

name: CF-Seg (Counterfactuals meet Segmentation)
what: Generates counterfactual images simulating how the same anatomy would look without disease (or without the perturbation) without changing anatomy, then segments with the unchanged model; improves anatomical segmentation on two real clinical chest X-ray datasets.
why_better: For a toxicity assay, counterfactual 'untreated appearance' images turn the segmentation model into a difference engine (segment treated, segment counterfactual-untreated, quantify what the toxin removed) - an explanation style the old plan's SHAP-only approach cannot produce, and one that maps directly onto the dose x time factorial design.
evidence: Two real-world clinical chest X-ray datasets; improvement in anatomical segmentation reported; exact numbers unverified (abstract only).
source_title: CF-Seg: Counterfactuals meet Segmentation (arXiv:2506.16213, Mehta, Ribeiro, Xia, Roschewitz, Santhirasekaram, Marshall, Glocker)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results)
fit_small_data: medium - the counterfactual generator is a separately trained generative model and is the data-hungry part of the pipeline; the segmentation side reuses the existing model.
fit_onnx_cpu: low - requires generative-model inference at analysis time, which is heavy for CPU-only desktop use.
risk: Relies on a generative model (verify it is not GAN-based against the project's no-GAN constraint); plausibility of counterfactual microscopy images is an open concern (raised for medical counterfactuals in MiMICRI, arXiv:2404.16174).

name: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) for segmentation masks and NTI
what: Post-hoc calibration procedure that bounds the expected value of any monotone loss (false-negative rate, distance/F1-style losses, graph distance) at a user-chosen level with an O(1/n)-tight guarantee, with extensions to distribution shift and cross-validation; companion post-hoc method 'Conformal Semantic Image Segmentation' (arXiv:2405.05145, CVPRW 2024) turns the same machinery into statistically valid prediction sets for segmentation masks.
why_better: Old plan's temperature scaling + ECE calibrates probabilities, not downstream risk; CRC gives finite-sample risk bounds on exactly the quantities the project cares about (e.g. expected neurite false-negative rate for thin 2-3 px tubes, or expected NTI error) - a guarantee level ECE cannot provide, which matters with only ~70 labelled images.
evidence: Theoretical: control tight up to O(1/n); worked examples in CV and NLP bound false negative rate, graph distance, token-level F1 (no image-segmentation-specific numbers in abstract).
source_title: Conformal Risk Control (arXiv:2208.02814, Angelopoulos, Bates, Fisch, Lei, Schuster)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results)
fit_small_data: high - post-hoc on a holdout or CV score set; a cross-validation variant exists for small n (Cross-Validation Conformal Risk Control, ISIT 2024).
fit_onnx_cpu: high - no model changes; only score calibration and threshold search at calibration time.
risk: With ~70 images the calibration split is tiny - must use the CV variant to avoid losing test data; coverage assumptions (exchangeability across doses/time points) need checking, e.g. per-dose calibration.

name: EQUIPS-style uncertainty propagation from segmentation to derived measurements
what: Workflow that Monte-Carlo samples the segmentation model (MC dropout / Bayesian CNN) into a per-pixel probability map, thresholds it at percentiles, and re-runs downstream quantity computation to build full uncertainty distributions of the derived measurements, using 3 percentile samples for approximately Normal cases and more for non-Normal tails.
why_better: Old plan reports the 4 morphometric parameters and NTI as point estimates; this workflow propagates segmentation uncertainty into neurite length, branch count, branch-angle distribution and soma morphology, so the 0/6/24 h dose effects are reported with honest confidence intervals and the paper can state when the distribution is non-Normal (bounding then fails).
evidence: 3D CT of woven composites, Li-ion battery electrodes, human torso (Nature Communications 2021): e.g. tortuosity uncertainty distribution non-Normal requiring ~10 percentile simulations vs 3 for Normal quantities; lower-quality image showed +22.2% std (conductivity) and +58.7% std (tortuosity) vs sharper image.
source_title: Quantifying the unknown impact of segmentation uncertainty on image-based simulations (Krygier et al., Nat Commun 12:5414)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results)
license: open access (Nature Communications, CC BY per publisher page)
fit_small_data: medium - needs T stochastic forward passes per image (MC dropout or 5-seed ensemble already in the old plan can supply samples).
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - T extra CPU forward passes per tile (T~10-20 is feasible offline); morphometry re-computation is cheap numpy/scikit-image work.
risk: Paper is 3D CT/image-based simulation; adaptation to 2D fluorescence/phase-contrast and graph-based morphometry (branch count, angles) is custom work; non-Normal distributions of branch-angle statistics may need many percentile samples.

name: Quantus (XAI evaluation toolkit with sanity checks and faithfulness metrics)
what: Python toolkit for systematically evaluating neural-network explanations: catalog of faithfulness, stability and sanity metrics (occlusion/AUC-based perturbation, etc.) plus implementations of the sanity-check tests (independence of model/data) for saliency methods.
why_better: Old plan ships 'SHAP-only XAI' with no evaluation of whether the attributions track the model at all; Quantus operationalizes the Adebayo et al. sanity checks and faithfulness metrics (e.g. AUC-based occlusion) on the segmentation attributions, converting 'we computed SHAP' into 'the attribution method passed/failed N quantitative checks'.
evidence: unverified (toolkit paper; no benchmark numbers in abstract).
source_title: Quantus: An Explainable AI Toolkit for Responsible Evaluation of Neural Network Explanations and Beyond (arXiv:2202.06861, Hedstrom et al.)
license: open source (PyPI package; exact license not checked)
fit_small_data: high - evaluation is post-hoc on the trained model; needs only the labelled validation split.
fit_onnx_cpu: medium - metrics require repeated forward passes with occluded/perturbed inputs; batch on CPU overnight if needed.
risk: Metric selection changes conclusions (some sanity checks are known to be contested - see 'Revisiting Sanity Checks for Saliency Maps', arXiv:2110.14297); dense-prediction metrics need masking adapted to soma/neurite anatomy.

name: Explainable Boosting Machines (EBM) with exact Shapley decomposition for the NTI
what: Glass-box additive model (GAM-style terms fitted by cyclic gradient boosting) whose predictions decompose into exact main and pairwise-interaction Shapley effects (no sampling); demonstrated on scientific image data tabularized with Gabor wavelets and on large-scale tabular insurance data.
why_better: Old plan's 'linear NTI then small NN' + KernelSHAP separates model from explanation and pays KernelSHAP approximation cost; EBM makes the NTI model itself the explanation: exact (not sampled) Shapley values, explicit dose x time interaction terms matching the 7x3 factorial design, and a continuous index instead of a linear baseline.
evidence: Car-insurance claims data (arXiv:2503.21321): evaluated on out-of-sample accuracy and calibration, exact main + pairwise interaction decomposition demonstrated, specific numbers not retrieved; cold-atom soliton images tabularized via Gabor wavelets (arXiv:2305.16526): explanations reported as consistent with human intuition, numbers unverified.
source_title: Extending Explainable Boosting Machines to Scientific Image Data (arXiv:2305.16526, Schug, Yerramreddy, Caruana, Greenberg, Zwolak); exact-Shapley property per 'Explainable Boosting Machine for Predicting Claim Severity and Frequency in Car Insurance' (arXiv:2503.21321)
code_url: none (no code link observed in search results; the interpret package is the common implementation but unverified here)
fit_small_data: high - only ~4-6 morphometric features; EBM is designed for small-feature settings, but 70 rows is a small sample, so assume few groups and pairwise interactions only.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - piecewise-polynomial basis scoring is trivial on CPU; ONNX export is a small custom re-implementation (few hundred lines).
risk: With 70 labelled samples EBM may underfit high-order interactions (dose x time x parameter); must be validated against the labelled unlabelled pool; if EBM accuracy is unacceptable, the fallback is the old small NN + exact Shapley only for the additive part.

name: Interpretable Machine Learning (Christoph Molnar, open textbook)
what: The standard open-access textbook on interpretable ML: model-agnostic methods (SHAP/SHAPley values, permutation importance, ALE, LOFO, ceteris paribus), simple interpretable models, and DNN-specific methods, each with strengths/weaknesses; 3rd edition adds LOFO and ceteris-paribus chapters.
why_better: Replaces the old plan's ad-hoc 'SHAP-only' usage with a complete, critically discussed method menu for the tabular NTI stage (including exact-Shapley-for-additive-models treatment), so the two-person team stops rediscovering pitfalls (baseline choice, interaction terms, dependency effects).
source_title: Interpretable Machine Learning: A Guide for Making Black Box Models Explainable (Christoph Molnar)
license: open access, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (stated on book site); edition year of 3rd edition unverified
fit_small_data: high - reference material; SHAP/additive-model chapters directly match the 4-parameter NTI problem.
fit_onnx_cpu: high - reference material; its recommended tabular methods (EBM, exact additive Shapley) are all CPU-trivial.
risk: none beyond keeping up with edition updates; some newer 2024-2026 evaluation work postdates the book.

name: xxAI - Beyond Explainable AI (Springer LNAI 13200)
what: 2022 Springer volume collecting peer-reviewed surveys of the XAI landscape: explanation methods, evaluation of explanations, and topics beyond explanation (trust, accountability), edited with contributions from the field's core groups.
why_better: Gives a 2022-dated, peer-reviewed map of XAI method families including XAI evaluation - exactly the gap in the old plan (which jumps from SHAP to deployment with no evaluation stage) - and it is free open access, so no licensing cost for a 2-person team.
source_title: xxAI - Beyond Explainable AI (Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence 13200, Springer)
license: open access (CC-BY per OpenAlex; also listed in OAPEN)
fit_small_data: high - reference material; its evaluation and reliability chapters guide the ~70-image validation protocol.
risk: survey coverage varies by chapter; not a how-to for implementation.

name: Explainable AI: Interpreting, Explaining and Visualizing Deep Learning (Samek, Montavon, Vedaldi, Hansen, Mueller; Springer LNCS 11700)
what: Foundational 2019 LNCS volume establishing the taxonomy and evaluation of interpretability, explanation and visualization methods for deep learning (attribution methods, visualization, evaluation protocols).
why_better: Provides the canonical taxonomy for choosing among attribution methods (Grad-CAM vs Integrated Gradients vs saliency/RISE) beyond the old plan's Captum defaults, with evaluation criteria the old plan omits; serves as the reference the TUSEB reviewers expect to be cited.
source_title: Explainable AI: Interpreting, Explaining and Visualizing Deep Learning (Samek et al., Lecture Notes in Computer Science 11700, Springer 2019)
license: closed access (Springer, TDM-only license per Crossref; not open access)
fit_small_data: high - reference material covering attribution methods applicable to the segmentation backbone.
risk: 2019 vintage: predates 2023-2026 evaluation tooling (Quantus, sanity-check follow-ups); buy/institutional access needed since not OA.

name: Explanatory Model Analysis (Biecek & Burzykowski)
what: 2021 CRC Press book on exploring, explaining and examining predictive models with explainable-ML methods (additive models, interaction effects, model-agnostic explanations).
why_better: Complements Molnar with a stronger focus on model examination and interaction terms, directly relevant to the tabular NTI stage where dose x time interactions must be visible to biologists; fills the 'examine the model' step the old plan lacks between 'linear NTI' and 'small NN'.
source_title: Explanatory Model Analysis (Piotr Biecek, Wiktor Burzykowski, CRC Press/Taylor & Francis)
license: closed access (Taylor & Francis, not open access per OpenAlex)
fit_small_data: high - reference material for the small-tabular NTI modelling stage.
risk: not open access - requires purchase or library access; overlaps ~60% with Molnar, so read selectively.
